answer: A small agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying reputation to slow, costly identity work: each new agent must hold its key through a probation ridge of graded epochs before it earns full voting weight, like goods clearing a wharf one crate at a time instead of flooding in; peers attest only to behavior they have watched for days, and a walnut-sized stake of earned rewards is burned on any proven fake, so mass fake accounts cost more than they could ever harvest.
